{
  "candidate_dispositions": [
    {
      "pressure_id": "constitutional_graph_pressure::direct_seed::bottlenecks",
      "disposition": "apply",
      "source_turn_numbers": [8, 12],
      "effect": "new_condition",
      "strongest_plausible_application": "The deployment exercise tests the 40-minute planning assumption, preventing a throughput failure if the physical barrier cannot match the evacuation speed.",
      "attempted_application_condition": "Deployment exercise must physically replicate nighttime/emergency conditions to validate the 40-minute threshold.",
      "why": "The system assumes a 40-minute window for deployment; verifying this is critical for actual performance.",
      "disposition_boundary": "Validation of the 40-minute window: if the drill fails this time, existing plans are insufficient.",
      "visible_effect": "Included a mandatory deployment exercise to reveal if the 40-minute window is a real bottleneck.",
      "private_guardrail": "Validating operational flow before project authorization."
    },
    {
      "pressure_id": "constitutional_graph_pressure::direct_seed::game-theory-payoffs",
      "disposition": "apply",
      "source_turn_numbers": [10, 12],
      "effect": "new_condition",
      "strongest_plausible_application": "The grant is forcing the city to expand scope; the mayor's office incentives conflict with the engineering peer-review timeline.",
      "attempted_application_condition": "New grant-funded expansions are conditioned on prior peer review.",
      "why": "The mayor's office frames extra anchors as free capacity; this is an incentive trap.",
      "disposition_boundary": "Refusal to accept new scope without equivalent review cycles.",
      "visible_effect": "Explicit decision to decline extra anchors without review.",
      "private_guardrail": "Decoupling grant availability from project scope."
    },
    {
      "pressure_id": "constitutional_graph_pressure::direct_seed::inversion",
      "disposition": "park",
      "source_turn_numbers": [8, 11],
      "effect": "uncertainty_change",
      "strongest_plausible_application": "If the barrier fails during an incident, is the failure due to equipment or operations?",
      "attempted_application_condition": "Documenting all 'operator delay' incidents.",
      "why": "Inversion is currently being addressed by the deployment exercise, but requires sustained evidence tracking during operations.",
      "disposition_boundary": "Post-incidenct review: failure to surface operator vs. equipment causes resets this pressure.",
      "visible_effect": "",
      "private_guardrail": ""
    },
    {
      "pressure_id": "constitutional_graph_pressure::direct_seed::systems-thinking",
      "disposition": "apply",
      "source_turn_numbers": [12],
      "effect": "reinforces_existing",
      "strongest_plausible_application": "Linking the barrier's performance to the drainage study prevents a 'quick fix' replacing long-term infrastructure.",
      "attempted_application_condition": "Drainage study must remain funded regardless of barrier performance.",
      "why": "Prevents the barrier from becoming an excuse to stop the comprehensive study.",
      "disposition_boundary": "The drainage study funding or timeline remains unchanged.",
      "visible_effect": "Mandating the drainage study continues on its schedule.",
      "private_guardrail": "Maintaining long-term feedback loops."
    },
    {
      "pressure_id": "constitutional_graph_pressure::direct_seed::incentives",
      "disposition": "apply",
      "source_turn_numbers": [10, 12],
      "effect": "new_condition",
      "strongest_plausible_application": "Grant money often distorts scope; this requires clear hard stops where the grant does not apply.",
      "attempted_application_condition": "Grant funding must not define the project scope.",
      "why": "Grant agency timing pressured the city to accept unreviewed blocks.",
      "disposition_boundary": "All scope changes must be cost-evaluated without grant urgency.",
      "visible_effect": "Rejection of the expanded scope despite grant availability.",
      "private_guardrail": "Standardizing decision criteria independent of grant cycles."
    },
    {
      "pressure_id": "constitutional_graph_pressure::direct_seed::margin-of-safety",
      "disposition": "apply",
      "source_turn_numbers": [11, 12],
      "effect": "new_condition",
      "strongest_plausible_application": "The warranty excludes deployment delays; this is a massive gap in the safety margin.",
      "attempted_application_condition": "Establishing a city-owned procedure for deployment that covers excluded warranty gaps.",
      "why": "Warranty as flood insurance error.",
      "disposition_boundary": "Explicit differentiation between equipment defect and city operational error in the contract.",
      "visible_effect": "Contract must explicitly separate equipment defect from deployment responsibility.",
      "private_guardrail": "Identifying liability gaps."
    },
    {
      "pressure_id": "constitutional_graph_pressure::graph_expansion::system-1",
      "disposition": "reject",
      "source_turn_numbers": [12],
      "effect": "no_material_effect",
      "strongest_plausible_application": "The system-1 bias occurred early (grant rush); it is now resolved by the move to a six-block, peer-reviewed scope.",
      "attempted_application_condition": "N/A",
      "why": "The decision process has been slowed significantly (drills, reviews).",
      "disposition_boundary": "Re-emergence of pressure to bypass review for speed.",
      "visible_effect": "",
      "private_guardrail": ""
    },
    {
      "pressure_id": "constitutional_graph_pressure::graph_expansion::confirmation-bias",
      "disposition": "apply",
      "source_turn_numbers": [8, 9],
      "effect": "new_condition",
      "strongest_plausible_application": "Auditing the 'industrial route vs. grocery access' distinction to avoid justifying the barrier with only favorable metrics.",
      "attempted_application_condition": "Service definitions must use consistent language across different user groups.",
      "why": "The memo language had a clear bias towards industrial transit over resident grocery access.",
      "disposition_boundary": "Consistency of impact language across all affected resident groups.",
      "visible_effect": "Requirement to keep consistent language for all impacted resident subgroups.",
      "private_guardrail": "Checking for bias in impact framing."
    },
    {
      "pressure_id": "constitutional_graph_pressure::graph_expansion::cognitive-load-theory",
      "disposition": "apply",
      "source_turn_numbers": [9],
      "effect": "new_condition",
      "strongest_plausible_application": "Residents are being offered a 'barrier' solution that doesn't simplify their incident load (grocery access).",
      "attempted_application_condition": "Incident response plan must be clearly defined for all affected parties.",
      "why": "Residents found the 'resilience' benefit confusing because it failed to account for their actual daily needs.",
      "disposition_boundary": "Operational clarity of the shuttle and emergency routing for all road users.",
      "visible_effect": "Integration of shuttle and emergency routing plans into the public deployment package.",
      "private_guardrail": "Ensuring the service plan addresses cognitive load."
    }
  ],
  "reconsidered_answer": "The final position is complete and defensible, provided the rigor established during the decision phase persists into operation. The authorization should link physical performance to city execution by mandate: every claim of 'protection' must be paired with the public incident plan (shuttle/emergency routes) and the peer-reviewed limits. Crucially, the deployment exercise must test the 40-minute planning assumption; failure here is a project-stopping event. Keep the drainage study funding and schedule independent of the barrier deployment. Distinguish equipment warranty from city operational responsibility in the contract, and acknowledge the uneven impact on grocery access with consistent language. The project is bounded by data, not the grant clock.",
  "change_summary": "Added a mandatory deployment drill condition to validate the 40-minute threshold and formalized the distinction between contract warranty and city operational liability.",
  "original_answer_preservation": "preserved"
}
